It examines whether many locally deciding robotic modules can produce a predictable, structurally qualified global body shape without surrendering load-transfer integrity, explicit human stop authority, module identity or full resource accounting. Its three-way coupling is Swarm Intelligence x Local Decision-Making x Global Safety. This is a hypothesis-forming research design, not a claimed roadworthy vehicle, passenger safety achievement or nanoscale-to-macroscale engineering demonstration. The preregistered candidate asks whether, under the same material, energy, computation, sensing, communication, operator and mission budgets, a frozen distributed morphology policy improves deadline-valid packet survival without worsening full-cycle mission energy. Strong competitors are tuned centralized predictive control, passive safe-hold modules, an ordinary local rule, and learned controllers protected by an equivalent independent safety shield. Concealed tests include false-status agents, split-brain groups, under-preloaded latches, weak-mode structural instability, old membership epochs, actuator saturation, unmetered field energy and false software stop acknowledgements. The treatment distinguishes mathematical guarantees conditional on assumptions from evidence about real machinery. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 separately paginated investigations spanning local policy and voting, physical load-bearing morphology, sensing and learning under uncertainty, global safety vetoes, fair causal baselines and cross-generation requalification. The 200 Research Gates carry independently identified failures, competing accounts, physical stop conditions and successor evidence packets; they are research invitations rather than completed results. Thirty-three distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos propose different physical instruments, calibration objects, safety-gate demonstrators and independent refusal replayers. The complete work preserves failed trials and abstentions instead of silently excluding them. This work is restricted to prospective non-occupancy engineering and makes no road-certification, crash-protection or full-sized autonomous vehicle claim. Relevant methodological evidence includes Robo-Matter (DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-53123-6), flying-swarm shape assembly (10.1038/s44172-026-00715-3), adaptive magnetic microrobots (10.1038/s41427-026-00682-3), safe multi-robot control review (10.1016/j.arcontrol.2024.100948), distributed control-barrier safety (10.1109/LRA.2024.3414268), changing-topology consensus (10.1109/TAC.2005.846556), and multi-agent adaptive safety (10.1109/ICRA57147.2024.10611037). papers.title: 車房結構健康自主監測極限 43/90 AUTONOMOUS STRUCTURAL HEALTH MONITORING OF MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT AUTONOMOUS STRUCTURAL HEALTH MONITORING OF MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition of the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 43 of 90). Its core coupling is Distributed Sensing x Fault Diagnosis x Predictive Maintenance. The book asks whether the physical health of a repeatedly moving and morphing modular habitat can be distinguished from normal changes in support, loading, geometry, temperature, humidity and measurement reference. The research setting is strictly scaled and unoccupied: instrumented panels, configurable hinges and locks, blind structural defects, environmental chambers and hardware-in-the-loop controllers. No habitable or road-certified mobile home is claimed. The falsifiable contract challenges a frozen diagnostic architecture against competent scheduled inspection, a calibrated classical modal detector and conventional condition-based maintenance under equal sensing, energy, time, human-operation and specimen budgets. It investigates damage-event recall, critical false release, detection timing, environmental normalization, sensor drift and physical-stop performance. The source Flagship 43 contract additionally specifies air-quality recovery without worsening false release; F43 preserves this as a separately tested environmental side constraint, not a substitute for structural load truth. Concealed challenges include fatigue cracks, loosened latches, sensor common-mode bias, unreported support changes, shifted water ballast, clock skew, missed communication packets, moisture leaks and hidden ventilation faults. An uncertain load path must result in an actual physical refusal, not a favourable aggregate health score. Thirty distinct mathematical research plates cover linearized structural dynamics, modal eigenproblems, hinge compliance, thermal strain correction, optical-fiber transfer, guided-wave time registration, graph observability, Kalman innovations, innovation covariance and statistical consistency, nonlinear filtering, Bayesian hypotheses, correlated uncertainty, change detection, complete-denominator fault recall, severe false-clear rates, competing-risk lifetime, fatigue propagation and noncompensatory bench-release conditions. Each plate defines its variables and units, derives or constructs a conditional model, identifies validity limits, gives a concrete blinded refutation and links to named chapters. The original source innovation, nu_k = y_k - H_k xhat_k_minus, is a residual relation for a declared observation mapping, not a guarantee of physical truth. Eighty-two chapters and 410 separately paginated investigations examine modular state identity, fold and support transitions, load redistribution, buried fatigue and joint damage, vibration and wave sensing, fiber and electrical transducers, environmental confounding, clock and calibration faults, latent-state filters, sensor network failure, uncertainty intervals, critical-recall performance, maintenance decisions and independent laboratory transfer. Two hundred individually differentiated Research Gates introduce concealed physical causes, fair mature comparators and coupled faults. Thirty-three distinguishable Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future instrument fixtures, reference transfer objects, structural stop witnesses, fault adjudicators and successor-ready evidence systems. They are proposed research capabilities, not claimed manufactured or externally validated devices. papers.title: 自主車房材料回收與微型製造極限 44/90 AUTONOMOUS MATERIAL RECYCLING AND MICROFABRICATION FOR MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT AUTONOMOUS MATERIAL RECYCLING AND MICROFABRICATION FOR MOBILE HABITATS AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition within the STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy (Research Institute XXXVI, Flagship 44 of 90). It asks whether retired modular components of an unoccupied morphing mobile-habitat research system can be identified, segregated, reclaimed and microfabricated into functionally qualified replacement specimens without concealing failed parts, external resources, unknown chemistry or damaged mechanical interfaces. Its core coupling is Material Circularity x Autonomous Microfabrication x Quality Control. All proposed studies use scaled, unoccupied coupons, guarded process enclosures and independently tested components. There is no claim of a finished nanorobotic factory, certified load-bearing building product or habitable mobile home. The research contract retains the original candidate that a frozen autonomous recovery-and-manufacturing process might reduce maintenance energy without worsening detection of dangerous faults. Because energy alone does not establish circular functionality, the design also requires directly measured received mass, polymer identity, real recyclate/virgin fraction, loss of molecular and reinforcement properties, extrusion and deposition quality, lower-tail mechanical strength, leakage, emissions, accepted-part yield and actual equipment shutdown. The strongest alternatives are competent professional recovery, conventional material reprocessing and functionally equivalent virgin replacement under the same test duty. Blinded trials include hidden mixed polymers, adhesive fragments, rehydrated PLA, unlogged extrusion heat, nozzle wear, short fiber attrition, buried layer voids, embrittled clips and omitted drying or reject-bin work. Every incomplete or quarantined part remains in the denominator. Thirty mathematically distinct research plates address material mass conservation, recycled-content ratios, sorting errors, grinding energy, moisture diffusion, time-temperature exposure, activated degradation, molecular mass retention, rheology, flow and heat transport, blend homogeneity, filtration, chain residence, deposition quality, interlayer fracture, void fraction, lower-tail mechanical testing, fatigue and creep, leakage, chemical emissions, acceptance sampling, correlated uncertainty, qualified yield, lifecycle energy and greenhouse accounting, physical stopping latency and noncompensatory release. The source contract's uncertainty model u_y^2 = J Sigma_x J^T + u_model^2 is retained with explicit correlated calibration assumptions; it is not proposed as a new law of recycling. Every equation includes a scope, units, a mechanism-specific blind challenge and links to research chapters. Eighty-two chapters and 410 separately paginated investigations develop seven linked scientific acts from source identity and safe disassembly through sorting and polymer chemistry, re-extrusion, microfabrication, mechanical and environmental qualification, complete physical/economic accounting, and interlaboratory replication. Two hundred Research Gates contain differentiated hidden interventions, conventional comparators and coupled failure tests. Thirty-three genuinely different Phoenix Answer Embryos propose prospective chemical assays, sorting witnesses, molecular-history archives, microextrusion fixtures, joint-test instruments, rejection interlocks, lifecycle ledgers and cross-generation evidence tools. These are hypotheses and experiment plans, not constructed devices or completed empirical results. This volume is a prospective non-occupancy research program. A recovered part must never be called safe because it looks geometrically correct, passes a single tensile coupon or receives a high digital-quality score. Component-method literature on circular additive manufacturing and repeated polymer reprocessing includes DOI 10.1016/j.jclepro.2020.121602, 10.1016/j.polymdegradstab.2022.109850, 10.1016/j.susmat.2025.e01430, 10.1016/j.rcradv.2026.200330, 10.1016/j.compositesa.2026.109603 and 10.3390/polym18172161. These sources do not validate this entire F44 architecture.
